data.description:
**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC1: ≥ 20 bundled NASA photos with attribution/licence; feeds AC6 evidence).

## Goal

As a player I want each level's backdrop to be a real NASA space photograph, and as the producer I want every bundled image traceable to its source and licence, so the game ships redistributable art with no runtime dependency on NASA services.

## Background

Producer answer Q1 (2026-10-25): **bundle** the photos as committed repo assets and **record attribution and licence** per image. Today the repo has no image-asset pipeline at all: the only image is the MenuScene GitHub-logo data URI (`src/assets/github-mark.svg`) and audio assets live in `public/audio`. Network access to NASA's images API was verified available from this host on 2026-10-28 (`https://images-api.nasa.gov/search?q=nebula` → `200`), and `ffmpeg` is installed locally, so resizing needs no new dependency.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `public/assets/backgrounds/` contains **≥ 20** committed NASA space photographs whose filenames match the texture keys from `src/data/backgrounds.ts` one-to-one (no orphan files, no missing files); each image is ≤ 1920×1080, and the whole directory is ≤ 5 MB (report the measured total in the completion comment).
2. `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` lists **every** image with: filename, NASA title/asset id, source URL, licence statement (US Government public-domain / NASA media-usage guidelines) and retrieval date; a per-image table with no gaps. The NASA media-usage URL is cited.
3. `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` (Node `fs`, no Phaser boot) enforces: file count ≥ 20, exact 1:1 key↔file match with the manifest, per-file and directory size budgets, image dimensions readable and ≤ 1920×1080 (JPEG/WebP header inspection or a tiny Node header parser — no new dependency), no byte-identical duplicate files, and an attribution row for every filename including a licence phrase.
4. No runtime NASA fetch: a test asserts no `nasa.gov`/`images-api` URL is reachable from `src/**` runtime code (documentation/attribution files and the dev-only fetch script are excluded), and the fetch/resize tooling lives outside the runtime entry graph.
5. `npm run build` (which includes `check-bundle-hygiene`) succeeds, and the assets are served from the built bundle (verified path: `dist/assets/backgrounds/…` or `dist/assets/…` depending on the chosen location, recorded in the completion comment).

6. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #1 — "At least 20 NASA space photos are bundled as game assets (public-domain / NASA-approved media) with attribution and licence notes; backgrounds render at the full 960×540 canvas (Phaser FIT scaling) and are a non-interactive layer that never occludes gameplay or intercepts input." — specifically the bundling + attribution half; the full-canvas non-interactive render half is AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` first with placeholder expectations, then add the images until it is green.
- Dev-time only script `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs`: query `https://images-api.nasa.gov`, download selected candidates into a temp dir, resize/compress with `ffmpeg` to ≤ 1920×1080 JPEG (quality ~80), emit `public/assets/backgrounds/<key>.jpg`. The script is tooling, never imported by `src/`.
- Curate for gameplay readability: dark, space-dominant, low-detail-in-the-middle images; reject anything that would fight the neon vector art.
- Write `ATTRIBUTION.md` from the metadata the script records (title/nasa_id/href/licence) so filenames cannot drift from attribution.
- Keep every asset under `public/assets/backgrounds/` (parent Key Files decision) so Phaser can load them by stable relative URL under Vite `base: './'`.

## Deliverables

- `public/assets/backgrounds/` — ≥ 20 compressed NASA photos.
- `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` — per-image source/title/licence table.
- `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs` — reproducible dev-time fetch/resize tooling.
- `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` — asset/attribution contract tests.

**Key Files:**

- `public/assets/backgrounds/ATTRIBUTION.md` — new directory holding the photos plus the attribution table.
- `public/assets/backgrounds/background-nebula-01.jpg` — one concrete example entry per bundled photo (≥ 20 files, keys from `src/data/backgrounds.ts`).
- `scripts/fetch-nasa-backgrounds.mjs` — new dev-only tooling.
- `src/data/backgrounds.assets.test.ts` — new asset contract tests.
- `src/data/backgrounds.ts` — texture keys / filename helper consumed by the tests (no edits expected unless the contract needs a helper).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: deterministic background manifest (texture keys + filename helper).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring needs the textures present for review).

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC1 non-interactive full-canvas layer, AC4 readability dimming, AC5 shared-core parity).

## Goal

As a player I want a dimmed space photo behind the neon gameplay at every level, and as a developer I want the background's create/dim/swap/destroy lifecycle to exist **once** in the shared combat core, so `PlayScene` and the gyms render identical backdrops and nothing intercepts input or leaks across restarts.

## Background

`PlayScene.create()` currently draws an inline black rectangle at `PLAYSCENE_BACKGROUND_DEPTH = -1000` (`src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`); `CombatScene` sets `backgroundColor: '#000000'` in its config block and `src/core/gameConfig.ts` uses `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR`. Gyms (`GymFormationScene`, `GymWeapons`, `GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility` — all `CombatScene` subclasses) draw no backdrop of their own. AGENTS.md requires shared behaviour to live once in `src/scenes/core/` and forbids forked copies; the repo-wide duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) enforces that.

Texture availability is the key design constraint: scene tests boot through `src/test/gameHarness.ts` (happy-dom, stubbed rendering) and cannot decode real JPEGs, so the layer must (a) accept an injected texture — tests register fixtures — and (b) degrade to the existing solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` backdrop when a key is absent, without stalling scene `create()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` owns the whole background lifecycle: create (image + dim overlay), `setLevel(level)` swap via `backgroundForLevel`, and `destroy()`; every tuning value (dim alpha/colour, nullable fallback colour, depth) is an exported constant — shared tuning lives in `src/core/constants.ts` — and no layering logic is duplicated in scenes.
2. Shared hooks on `CombatCoreScene` (`_createBackground()`, `_setBackgroundLevel(level)`, and teardown inside the existing `teardownRunState()`), so `PlayScene` and every `CombatScene` gym call the **same** code; `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (duplicate-body guard) passes with no allow-list additions.
3. The background renders full-canvas at 960×540 (`setOrigin(0)`, display size `GAME_WIDTH × GAME_HEIGHT`, `scrollFactor(0)`), sits at depth ≤ −1000 (below gameplay at 0 and the juice layers at −10…−7) and is **non-interactive**: no input handlers are attached and pointer/keyboard input reaches the gameplay layer — asserted by test during a live scene tick.
4. Readability: a dim overlay (exported alpha/tint) sits above the photo and below gameplay so enemies, bullets and the player stay legible; when no texture is available the layer renders the solid `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback instead (no throw, no repeated warning spam).
5. Missing-texture safety and no-stall guarantee: booting `PlayScene` (and one gym) in the test harness with **no** background textures registered completes `create()` and ticks without error, and a subsequent `setLevel()` with a registered fixture texture swaps to that texture — both tested.
6. `PlayScene` uses the shared layer instead of its inline black rectangle (initial level from `waveManager.level`), and the layer is destroyed on shutdown/restart so no display object survives into the next run — tested via the scene-restart path.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #4 — "Gameplay readability is preserved: backgrounds are dimmed/desaturated beneath the neon vector art so enemies, bullets and the player ship stay legible (GDD §7.1 aesthetic, "2.5× keeps bullets legible against the neon background")." — specifically the dimming/readability rule, plus the full-canvas non-interactive layer from parent AC #1 and the shared-core home from parent AC #5; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Consume the shared `src/test/backgroundFixtures.ts` helper from the manifest slice (do not fork texture stubs); write the unit tests before the implementation.
- `backgroundLayer.ts`: a small handle class `{ image, dim, setLevel, destroy, textureKey() }`; `setLevel` no-ops when the key is unchanged (idempotent), destroys nothing when the fallback is in use.
- Add the hooks on `CombatCoreScene` next to `resetRunState`/`teardownRunState`; wire the teardown call once so subclasses get it for free.
- Replace `PlayScene`'s inline rectangle with `_createBackground()` / `_setBackgroundLevel(this.waveManager.level)`; delete the now-unused local depth constant **only** if nothing else references it (report rather than silently drop dead code otherwise).
- Do not add warp/transition logic here — that is the next slice; this slice proves static per-level rendering, dimming, non-interactivity and teardown.

## Deliverables

- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` + `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.test.ts`.
- Shared hooks/constants in `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` and `src/core/constants.ts`.
- `PlayScene` initial-background wiring (no level-change swap yet).

**Key Files:**

- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.ts` — new shared lifecycle module (create/dim/swap/destroy).
- `src/scenes/core/backgroundLayer.test.ts` — new unit tests (depth, non-interactive, fallback, teardown, idempotent swap).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — shared `_createBackground`/`_setBackgroundLevel` hooks + teardown.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — replace the inline backdrop rectangle with the shared layer.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — dim/tint/depth tuning constants; `GAME_BACKGROUND_COLOR` fallback.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity/duplicate-body guard (read-only unless the guard legitimately needs the new shared surface listed).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95 (deterministic background manifest + fixture harness); AH-0MVSEB2WZ000MZY8 (real imagery — the layer itself works with fixture textures).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring); AH-0MVSEC0J0004YNJC (gym parity verification).

**Parent:** AH-0MVIB7PD50029ZY1 — Background scenes (covers parent AC3: unmistakable warp transition timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS`; related to AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU "unmistakable" bar).

## Goal

As a player I want an unmistakable hyperspace "warp" when the background changes between levels, and as a developer I want that effect to be a deterministic, time-boxed, individually switchable module with a testable timeline, so level changes read as a jump through space without ever hurting readability or blocking play.

## Background

Producer answer Q2 (2026-10-25): **Option A — hyperspace-style one-shot** (converging streak overlay + radial scale distortion + brief flash/crossfade), timed to `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s, currently exported from `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`). Existing VFX modules show the house pattern to copy: exported tuning constants plus per-layer `*_ENABLE_*` toggles and caller-owned effect registries that are destroyed on `SHUTDOWN` (`src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts`, `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts`, `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts`).

Import direction matters: `PlayScene` imports VFX modules, so a VFX module must **not** import `PlayScene`. The duration therefore moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and is re-exported from `PlayScene` for existing importers.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` moves to `src/core/constants.ts` and `PlayScene` re-exports it unchanged, so `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` can derive `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` from the same single source (no duplicated literal); all existing importers (`PlayScene.test.ts`, `SceneNavigation.test.ts`) keep compiling without edits.
2. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` exposes the full timeline as exported constants (streak phase, distortion/scale phase, flash/crossfade phase) whose phases are ordered, non-overlapping and sum to the total duration; a test asserts the sum and ordering so the effect can never outlive the transition window.
3. The effect renders three layers — converging streak overlay, radial scale distortion, brief flash/crossfade into the incoming background — each with its own `BACKGROUND_WARP_ENABLE_*` toggle (following the `ENDOFRUN_ENABLE_*` pattern) and exported magnitudes (streak count, speed, colours, scale range, flash alpha).
4. Deterministic: no `Math.random()` (or a seeded generator) — two runs from the same inputs produce byte-identical layer parameters, asserted by test. Time-boxed and observable: an `update(dt)`-style tick API (no reliance on wall-clock tweens) so a test can advance exactly `BACKGROUND_WARP_DURATION_SECONDS` and assert completion; `isComplete()` is true at the end and never before.
5. Bounded and disposable: a fixed maximum streak count (constant), all display objects inside one container, `destroy()` idempotent, and a test asserts the container/children are gone after completion and after an early `destroy()` (no leaks if the scene restarts mid-warp).
6. `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` covers the ACs above; changed-scope tests and `tsc --noEmit` pass.

7. **Parent-AC traceability:** this slice's primary implementation is parent AC #3 — "A "warp" transition effect plays while backgrounds change — timed to the existing `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (1.5 s) transition pause — after which the new level's background is fully shown; the effect is deterministic, time-boxed, and does not block input or wave progression." — specifically the warp effect module itself (deterministic, time-boxed, switchable); the non-blocking wiring is AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD; the remaining ACs of this slice are the verification and the collateral work it needs.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write the test file first against the constant/API surface you intend to ship (red → green).
- Implement the effect as Phaser `Graphics` inside a `Container` at a depth just above the background layer and below gameplay (exported depth constant); no new assets and no new dependencies.
- Choose deterministic pseudo-randomness from a small in-module LCG seeded by `(fromLevel, toLevel)` so each level pair looks slightly different but reproducible — never `Math.random()`.
- Drive animation from an explicit `update(dt)`/`tick` call (the scene's `update` feeds it) rather than `this.tweens`, matching the deterministic-boot test harness in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`.
- Keep it visually consistent with `wormholeSpawn`/`phaseShiftJuice` (violet→cyan converging lines, white flash peak).
- Do not trigger it from a scene here — the wiring slice owns the trigger; this slice ships the module plus tests.

## Deliverables

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — deterministic, switchable hyperspace warp effect with exported timeline.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — timeline, determinism, completion, toggle and teardown tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` relocated (single source of truth).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export only (no behaviour change).

**Key Files:**

- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.ts` — new warp transition module.
- `src/vfx/backgroundWarp.test.ts` — new tests.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` + warp depth/colour constants.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — re-export `LEVEL_TRANSITION_SECONDS` (no logic change).
- `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.ts` / `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — patterns to mirror (read-only).
- `src/vfx/phaseShiftJuice.ts` — visual-language reference (read-only).

## Dependencies

- Depends on: AH-0MVSEASIM005TU95 (deterministic background manifest — level identifiers/seeding only).
- Blocks: AH-0MVSEBW8L009O3JD (PlayScene level-change wiring).
- Related: AH-0MVNTR89P0022JIU (unmistakable phase-shift/wormhole effects) — same producer bar, coordinate the visual language; this slice must not weaken that item's effect.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome
resolver": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New Phaser-free pure module `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` owning the wheel's
mathematics and the single reward-application entry point, so `PlayScene` and
any gym consume identical code (gym↔game parity, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1). The
scene never computes probabilities — it receives the resolved outcome.

## Design

- `MINI_BOSS_WHEEL_SLOT_COUNT = 100`; the distribution is a single named
  constant: 1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single.
- `buildWheelWedges(ownedKinds)` → one wedge per owned permanent kind plus one
  bonus wedge, in a stable order (weapons first, then power-ups, matching
  `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`).
- `drawWheelOutcome(slotIndex, ownedKinds)` → a resolved outcome
  `{ gains: Array<{ id, levels }> }` for a slot index 0–99 drawn by the
  caller's injected run-seeded RNG (single/double/triple/bonus). A
  multi-upgrade slot selects **distinct** owned kinds where possible, repeating
  a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count.
- `applyWheelOutcome(outcome, effectsRegistry, player)` → applies every gain
  exactly once through the shared `applyMineralChoiceReward` seam (one
  `weapon-level`/`power-up-level` choice-option per level-gain step), so the
  awarded levels run the identical permanent-level machinery as the hold-full
  choice.
- **No level-cap filtering** — parity with `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`, which
  offers level-ups with no cap check; every level always counts (see parent
  OPEN QUESTION 1).
- Module-level JSDoc documents the distribution, the distinct-pick rule and
  the "a mini-boss always pays out" invariant (parent AC3/AC4).

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (new)
- `src/powerups/choiceReward.ts` (consumed unchanged — shared reward seam)
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` (`buildLevelUpOption` / `toChoiceOption` consumed)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolveSlotState().ownedIds` feeds the wedge list)
- `src/powerups/__tests__/miniBossWheel.test.ts` (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"
- Blocks: "Launcher-agnostic mini-boss wheel overlay scene", "Rework PlayScene
  mini-boss reward to the wheel"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC3, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` is a pure, Phaser-free **shared module** exporting the **100-slot distribution** (1 bonus / 5 triple / 10 double / 84 single) from a single named constant, and a weighted outcome resolver over the owned permanent kinds.
- Outcomes are drawn from the **run-seeded RNG** (injectable, no `Math.random()`, no wall clock) so the same seed and owned-kind snapshot reproduce the same outcome.
- Multi-upgrade slots pick **distinct** owned kinds where possible and repeat a kind only when there are fewer owned kinds than the slot's count (one owned kind landing a 3-slot gains +3 levels on it).
- The bonus outcome resolves to +1 level on every owned permanent kind.
- A single shared application entry point applies a resolved outcome exactly once through `applyMineralChoiceReward`, so the distribution/resolver and the reward application live in shared modules the game and gyms both consume.
- The wedge list and the weighted outcome are derived from the same owned-kind snapshot (`resolveSlotState().ownedIds`); the module never requires a scene or a Phaser type and never computes probabilities for display.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin
behaviour": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New launcher-agnostic wheel overlay scene `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`
mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s overlay pattern (pause, single optional
result callback, demo auto-select contract). The scene receives the owned-kind
wedges and a resolved outcome from the launcher; it only animates and reports,
never computes probabilities.

## Design

- Registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` so `scene.launch('MiniBossWheelScene',
  …)` works everywhere.
- Payload: `wedges` (one per owned permanent kind + bonus wedge, each carrying
  the code-drawn icon + display name), `outcome` (target wedge index + extra
  gained wedges for multi-upgrade spins), optional `onResult` callback
  (mirrors `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), and optional `autoSpinMs`
  (demo mode: after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) / `fireSchedule` (reduced-
  volume ghost fire while paused, reusing the shared hold-full metronome).
- Spin: pointer click or any keyboard key starts a fast-start, ease-out
  rotation (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported
  as a constant) that stops on the target wedge; the landed wedge is
  highlighted; the result callback fires exactly once; a later spin is a
  no-op.
- **Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer Q2):** when the outcome grants 2–3
  kinds, the landing wedge renders **all** the gained kinds' icons inside that
  one wedge ("all icons present") — the other gained kinds are not lit up on
  separate wedges — so the complete result is legible at the pointer.
- Tension over predictability: the wedge list order and the target angle are
  hidden from the player until the spin stops (outcome resolved by the
  launcher from the run-seeded RNG before launch).
- Code-first visuals only (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` (register the scene)
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` (reused unchanged)
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution, consumed unchanged)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MiniBossWheelScene.test.ts` (paired test item)

## Dependencies

- Blocked by: "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin behaviour" and "Pure
  wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"
- Blocks: "Rework PlayScene mini-boss reward to the wheel", "Prove gym↔game
  parity for the mini-boss wheel reward"
- Related: parent AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD (AC1, AC2, AC6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- A wheel overlay scene exists (`src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`), registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts`, presenting **one wedge per owned permanent kind** across the shared six-slot pool (power-up kinds **and** weapon drops) **plus a single bonus wedge**, drawn with the existing code-drawn icons; the upgrade-or-unlock menu is never shown through this surface.
- Play is paused exactly like the hold-full choice while the overlay is open, and the overlay closes and gameplay resumes when the result callback completes.
- Spinning is **player-initiated** (click/keyboard): the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported as a constant), the outcome is not predictable until it stops, and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.
- A **multi-upgrade outcome's landing wedge shows all the gained kinds' icons** in that one wedge (producer answer Q2 — "the wedge with the multi-results has all icons present"), with no separate highlights on other wedges, and the whole outcome applied exactly once.
- Level-saturated kinds are **not** filtered out of the draws (producer answer Q1 = Option A): the wheel matches the hold-full choice and a spin always increments levels.
- The scene is launcher-agnostic: it receives the wedges and the resolved outcome, exposes a **single optional result callback** (mirroring `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), never computes probabilities itself, and never reaches into a launcher by key.
- Demo mode auto-spins after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot never stalls; normal play waits for input.
- The paired test item's tests pass and the changed-scope gate is green.

# Wrap-aware steering and clearance

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC1.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player watching the attract demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge
to reach a target that is closer the other way, instead of treating the four
seam edges as walls it must not approach, so its movement looks like a human's
and it stops camping near walls it wrongly fears.

## Context

Both steering evaluators reject a bearing purely because it reaches an edge
inside `wallMargin`:

- legacy `evaluateVector` — `src/ai/botDecision.ts` ("reaches a wall within
  `wallMargin`", `wallMargin: 40` default);
- competent `evaluateDirection` — `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`
  ("Walls: reject a bearing that reaches an edge inside the wall margin",
  `wallMargin: 30` default).

Both also derive the objective bearing from the raw straight line, so a
seam-crossing route to an objective is never even considered. The playfield
genuinely wraps: the player ship wraps at all four edges
(`src/utils/movementModel.ts`), bullets wrap (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`),
and wrap-aware enemies now fly over the edges too (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

This slice consumes the primitives from the wrap-geometry child
(AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG's wrap-geometry primitive child) — no seam maths is written
here.

## Scope

1. Remove the wall test from both evaluators: an edge is no longer a hazard, so
   `evaluateVector`/`evaluateDirection` never mark a bearing unsafe merely for
   reaching an edge. Keep clearance meaningful: the distance-to-edge term stays
   only as a *clearance* contribution if it is still useful, and if it is dropped
   the clearance cap semantics are preserved.
2. Steering objectives use the **shortest wrapped path**: the objective bearing
   fed to the fan is computed with the wrapped delta (raw vs. seam-crossing
   duplicate of the objective, whichever is shorter), with the near-tie
   hysteresis from the geometry child so the chosen duplicate does not flip
   every tick.
3. Edge-crossing motion is used deliberately when net-positive (Q2 in the
   parent Appendix) — it falls out of shortest-path selection; no scripted wrap
   manœuvre and no change to the human-like governor
   (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`).
4. Update the existing integration assertion in
   `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` that presumes the bot "never wraps
   the screen" (the brake-to-stop case) so it still asserts a controlled stop
   without asserting the bot cannot cross a seam; add seam scenarios instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The four arena edges stop being walls in the steering safety/clearance test:
   neither the legacy `evaluateVector` (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) nor the
   competent `evaluateDirection` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`)
   rejects a direction solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`; a
   unit test per evaluator drives a bearing straight at each of the four edges
   from mid-playfield and asserts `safe === true`.
2. Steering toward an objective uses the shortest wrapped path: when the
   seam-crossing route to the objective is shorter than the raw line, the chosen
   bearing points at the wrapped duplicate; when the raw line is already
   shortest, the chosen bearing is unchanged from today's behaviour.
3. Unit tests cover **each of the four edges** (left/right/top/bottom): the
   wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter, and an edge-crossing direction
   is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.
4. Hysteresis at nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths: a test drives a sequence of
   ticks where the two route lengths swap by a tiny margin each tick and asserts
   the committed objective duplicate does not oscillate.
5. The human-like governor's reaction cadence, W/A/D control mapping and human
   thrust presses are unchanged; existing steering/bot integration tests stay
   green apart from the deliberately updated "never wraps" assertion, which is
   re-stated as "still brakes to a controlled stop".
6. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `bearingTo`,
  `chooseSteeringDirection`.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `evaluateVector` and the legacy target-bearing path.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts` — per-edge wrap tests (written first).
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — updated "never wraps" assertion plus
  seam-crossing scenarios.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — wrap scenario.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child (shared wrapped delta/bearing +
hysteresis must exist first).

## Out of scope

`wallMargin` removal from tunables, style fitting and the tuning UI (separate
child); aim/intercept, nearest-selection, threat prediction and eval parity
(separate children).

# Seam-aware aim and intercept

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC2
(aim half).

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge
— so engagements play out across the whole wrap-around arena.

## Context

Aim maths is raw Euclidean today:

- `bearingTo` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) — `normalise(to - from)`;
- `interceptPoint` (same module) — lead solve on raw deltas;
- the legacy aim/aim-delta path in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `atan2` on raw
  deltas.

The enemy side already aims on the torus via `aimVectorToTarget` /
`wrappedAxisDelta` (`src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`, used by
`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`), so the bot currently fights a wrap-aware opponent
with a wrap-blind gun — a systematic disadvantage once enemy wrap lands.

## Scope

1. `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint` compute their deltas along the shortest
   wrapped path (per-axis wrapped delta), with the bot's
   `playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`; both accept the wrap model without
   changing their existing signatures' call sites more than necessary (a
   `WrapWorld`/tunables argument).
2. The intercept solve predicts the target on the torus: the predicted point is
   the target's position advanced by its velocity, then the *route* to it is the
   shortest wrapped one, so a lead solution that must cross a seam is still
   produced. Stationary targets reduce exactly to the wrapped bearing.
3. Legacy aim in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` uses the same shared wrapped maths
   (delegating to the shared module, no second implementation).
4. Behaviour is bit-identical when the raw line is already the shortest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware aim and targeting — aim and target selection run on the torus: `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path.
2. Aim runs on the torus: `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) and the legacy aim compute in
   `src/ai/botDecision.ts` compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path, using
   the shared wrap-geometry primitives (no copied seam maths).
3. When the wrapped route to a target is shorter than the raw line, the returned
   aim angle equals the wrapped-path angle (test asserts the exact expected
   heading for a target across each of the four edges); firing off one edge
   arrives from the opposite edge.
4. When the raw line is already shortest, the aim angle is unchanged from the
   pre-change behaviour (regression test on a representative non-seam geometry).
5. `interceptPoint` leads a moving target across the seam: a test with a target
   whose velocity carries it over an edge returns the wrapped intercept point and
   converges (iteration count honoured), while a stationary target reduces to the
   wrapped bearing.
6. The legacy decision layer's aim output is byte-for-byte the pre-change value
   for a non-seam geometry (golden assertion in `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`).
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Goal

Make the temporary window (TTL) a **per-upgrade data property** instead of
"the effect duration applies only to timed kinds" (parent decision 1, AC2).

**User story:** as the balance owner I want each upgrade entry to declare how
long a field-pickup level lasts, so retuning a window is a catalogue edit and
no single global constant governs every power-up.

## Required behaviour

- `PowerUpEntry` gains a temporary-window TTL field in **seconds** (name it
  `temporaryWindow` to match the existing `tempWindow` vocabulary).
- The seven instant kinds declare their own value in `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`:
  `bomb` 10, `smart_bomb` 10, `strike` 10, `phase_shift` 15, `teleport` 15,
  `extra_life` 10, `mystery_ufo` 15 (producer-approved starting values;
  deliberately short so a temporary level cannot compound across a wave).
- A single resolver, exported next to the catalogue, returns the TTL for a
  field pickup of `id`:
  - **timed kinds** → the level-resolved effect duration already used by
    `_applyTimedEffect` (`stats.shieldDuration`, `stats.speedDuration`,
    `P_FRENZY_DURATION`-family, `forceFieldDuration`, magnet/scoop 15 s, …),
    so behaviour is unchanged and the window stays level-scaled;
  - **instant kinds** → the catalogue `temporaryWindow`;
  - the resolver never returns `undefined` for a kind in
    `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS` (fail loudly if a new instant kind forgets its TTL).
- The existing `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) stays the **default** weapon TTL,
  surfaced through the same resolver shape so a future weapon definition can
  declare its own window (no behaviour change in this item).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **TTL is defined per upgrade, not globally.** Timed effects keep their
  level-resolved effect duration as the window; each instant kind declares its
  own TTL in the shared catalogue (no single hard-coded constant applies to
  every power-up), and every one of the seven instant kinds carries its value.
- AC2 — A single exported resolver returns the field-pickup TTL for a
  power-up id, composing the existing level-resolved stats for timed kinds and
  the catalogue value for instant kinds; no new hard-coded cross-kind constant
  exists anywhere in `src/`.
- AC3 — Tests assert the exact per-kind TTL values for the seven instant
  kinds, and assert that a level-scaled timed effect (shield 15 s → 30 s at a
  higher level) keeps its level-scaled window through the resolver.
- AC4 — A unit test proves the TTL is data-driven: changing a catalogue entry's
  TTL changes the resolved window with no code change (test-time override, not
  a copied constant).
- AC5 — A test asserts the resolver returns a finite, positive value for every
  `POWER_UP_LEVEL_IDS` entry (a future kind that forgets its TTL turns the
  suite red).
- AC6 — No behaviour change is introduced by this item; it is purely additive
  data plus a resolver, consumed by the window implementation item.

## Constraints

- TTL values live in the catalogue (`src/powerups/types.ts`), not in
  `src/core/constants.ts`; no per-kind `switch` in a scene or gym.
- Do not change how the timed kinds' windows are currently started/expired —
  this item only exposes the value through a shared resolver.
- Numeric values are balance tuning: document them as such in the catalogue
  comment.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `PowerUpEntry.temporaryWindow`, the seven
  instant-kind values, catalogue comment on tuning.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — re-export/companion of the shared TTL
  resolver alongside `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (timed-kind duration lookup).
- `src/powerups/types.test.ts` — per-kind TTL assertions and data-driven
  override test.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `WEAPON_TIMEOUT_MS` documented as the default
  weapon TTL (no value change).

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC (AC2, Resolved decision 1).
- Depends on: AH-0MVUGI3BF00423OO (red contract tests).
data.title: F2: Per-upgrade temporary-window TTL in the catalogue

data.description:
## Goal

Give every **instant-effect** field pickup a real temporary window so its
temporary level component always reverts (parent AC1, the core defect).

**User story:** as the player, when I collect a temporary version of an item I
already own permanently, the extra level must last only as long as that
pickup's window and then revert to my permanent level — exactly as it does for
the timed kinds.

## Required behaviour

In the shared `EffectsRegistry` (single implementation for `PlayScene`, every
gym and the headless arena):

- A **field pickup** (`applyCollect(id, false)`) of an instant kind
  (`bomb`, `smart_bomb`, `strike`, `phase_shift`, `teleport`, `extra_life`,
  `mystery_ufo`) opens a temporary window sized by the AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A resolver, through
  the existing `_startOrRefreshTimed` machinery, while keeping every existing
  one-shot/consumable behaviour:
  - `bomb`/`smart_bomb` still queue exactly one pulse;
  - `strike` still queues exactly one bolt;
  - `mystery_ufo` still queues exactly one drone spawn;
  - `phase_shift`/`teleport`/`extra_life` still grant their consumables via
    the level store (the grant is *not* deferred to the window).
- At window expiry the existing `_expireTimedEffect` path runs
  (`clearTemporary` → effective level reverts to the permanent level, or the
  item becomes inactive when no permanent grant was earned) and, for
  `phase_shift`, the existing re-arm cooldown behaviour is unchanged.
- A **permanent** (hold-full) grant of an instant kind opens **no** window and
  must not resurrect one; it keeps its current permanent-flag behaviour.
- A re-collection during an open window refreshes it to the full TTL (never
  additive), matching the timed kinds.
- `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)` reports the remaining window for these kinds
  so the HUD can render a countdown instead of `∞` while it is open.

## Queued one-shot risk (must be closed)

`strike` keeps a decided bolt **latched** across frames until the shared core
acknowledges it, and `CombatCoreScene._updateOrbitalStrike` reads
`registry.strikeDamage()` at landing time — after the window may have expired.
Capture the level-resolved strike damage when the bolt is decided (latch time)
and return that captured value from `strikeDamage()` (or an equivalent
decision-time snapshot) so a reverted level can never weaken or re-price an
already-decided bolt. The same "resolve once, at decision time" rule applies to
the bomb/smart-bomb pulse stats that are read on the frame the pulse fires.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **No temporary level is immortal.** After a field pickup of any kind
  the temporary level component is removed at its per-upgrade TTL and the
  effective level reverts to the permanent level (or the item becomes
  inactive/unowned). Covers the seven instant kinds and the already-timed
  kinds; proven by the red contract table turning green.
- AC2 — A permanent (hold-full) grant of an instant kind opens no temporary
  window: `powerUpTemporaryRemaining(id)` stays `undefined` and the item never
  silently expires.
- AC3 — Existing one-shot semantics are preserved and asserted: one bomb pulse
  per field pickup, one smart-bomb pulse, one orbital bolt, one drone spawn,
  and the level-derived consumable grants still land immediately.
- AC4 — A latched orbital strike uses the damage resolved **when the bolt was
  decided**; a test latches a bolt, expires the window, then resolves and
  asserts the pickup-time damage was applied.
- AC5 — Re-collecting during an open window refreshes to the full TTL rather
  than stacking windows; two windows never compete (one timer per kind).
- AC6 — The window start/expire code lives only in the shared registry; no
  scene or gym duplicates it, and the parity/equivalence guards still pass.

## Constraints

- Reuse `_startOrRefreshTimed` / `_expireTimedEffect` / `clearTemporary`; do
  not add a parallel timer map or a second lifecycle.
- No per-kind scene timers; no new global duration constant (TTL comes from
  the AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A resolver).
- Consumables already granted are never clawed back on expiry (AH-0MVUGI4WG008HU3M asserts it;
  do not add rollback logic here).

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — window start for instant kinds, latch-time
  strike-damage snapshot, expiry bookkeeping.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — per-kind window/revert and one-shot
  preservation tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — orbital-strike seam consumes the
  decision-time damage (no behaviour change beyond the snapshot).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts` — AH-0MVUGI3BF00423OO table turns green.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.test.ts` — latched-bolt damage test.

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC (AC1, Resolved decision 1).
- Depends on: AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (per-upgrade TTL resolver).
- Supersedes the "Resolved decision 4: no temporary window" note from
  AH-0MUX802450085VZZ.
data.title: F3: Instant-kind temporary windows and revert at expiry

data.description:
## Goal

A permanent (hold-full) grant applied while a field-pickup window is open must
never strand the temporary component (parent AC3, producer Q3 answer).

**User story:** as the player, if I earn the permanent upgrade while a
temporary pickup is still running, my level must settle on the permanent level
— it must not keep a free extra level for the rest of the run.

## Required behaviour

Two paths, one rule: the effective level after the window closes equals the
permanent level, and `getTempStacks(id)` / `getTempWeaponStacks(id)` are `0`.

- **Power-ups** (`PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, true)` + `EffectsRegistry`
  `_startOrRefreshTimed`): keep today's "the existing window is left to expire
  on its own schedule" behaviour — but only if the window really does expire.
  Document the contract on `collect` and assert it for every kind (the AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ
  windows make it true for the instant kinds; the timed kinds already behave
  this way). A permanent grant must never cancel an open window's expiry.
- **Weapons** (`Player.equipWeapon(id, true)`): today it deletes
  `_weaponTimers` (stopping the countdown) and leaves `_tempWeaponStacks`,
  which makes a field pickup permanent. Clear the temporary stacks for that
  weapon in the permanent branch so the level settles on the permanent grant.
  The effective level is unchanged by the clear (the permanent grant already
  raised the permanent component by one), and the countdown correctly
  disappears because a permanent weapon has no window (`∞` in the HUD).
  Document this choice in the `equipWeapon` doc comment as the strategy
  required by AC3 (immediate clear rather than keep-the-window), since the
  weapon timer is what carries the window.
- Add a defensive guard/assertion so any future third write path cannot leave
  a temporary stack without a window to expire it (a store-level helper such as
  `clearTemporary(id)` called from the permanent branch is acceptable; no new
  parallel counter).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Permanent grant never leaves a stale temporary stack.** A hold-full
  reward applied while a field-pickup window is active leaves the effective
  level at the permanent level for every power-up kind: either the window is
  kept and expires (clearing the temporary component) or the component is
  cleared immediately; `getTempStacks(id)` ends at `0`.
- AC2 — For every timed weapon: field pickup → permanent grant mid-window →
  `getWeaponLevel(id) === getPermanentWeaponLevel(id)` and
  `getTempWeaponStacks(id) === 0`, both immediately after the grant and after
  ticking the weapon timers far beyond the window.
- AC3 — The permanent weapon grant still sets the weapon active, primary and
  ready-to-fire, and the HUD weapon row reads `∞` (no countdown) afterwards.
- AC4 — A test asserts the chosen strategy explicitly (weapon: temporary stack
  cleared at grant time; power-up: window kept and expired), so the two
  behaviours are documented as intentional rather than accidental.
- AC5 — `PowerUpLevelStore.collect(id, permanent)` and
  `Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` doc comments state the contract; no
  second counter, map or timer is introduced.
- AC6 — The red contract table's "permanent grant mid-window" cases pass.

## Constraints

- Weapons and power-ups keep their existing single source of truth
  (`Player._permanentWeaponGrants`/`_tempWeaponStacks` and
  `PowerUpLevelStore._permanentGrants`/`_tempStacks`).
- Do not change how the hold-full choice prices levels (permanent only); this
  item only removes a stranded temporary component.
- `resetWeapon()` and `resetWeaponLevels()` semantics are unchanged.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — permanent `equipWeapon` branch clears
  `_tempWeaponStacks`; doc comment states the AC3 strategy.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — permanent-grant-mid-window weapon tests.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `collect` contract comment + any guard.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — store-level mid-window grant tests.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts` — AH-0MVUGI3BF00423OO mid-window cases.

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC (AC3, Resolved decision 3, producer Q3).
- Depends on: AH-0MVUGI3Q4009MW6A (TTL resolver; the power-up half of the assertion needs AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ's
  windows for the instant kinds).
data.title: F4: Permanent grant never strands a temporary stack

data.description:
## Goal

Prove — and where necessary fix — that reverting a temporary level leaves the
player's consumables, the HUD and the six-slot loadout in a consistent state
(parent AC4, AC5, AC6).

**User story:** as the player, when my temporary level reverts I keep the lives,
Phase Shift charges and teleports I already earned, the HUD tells me the truth
(effective level with a countdown, then `∞`), and a freed slot comes back.

## Required behaviour

- **Consumables persist (AC4).** `PowerUpLevelStore.clearTemporary(id)` keeps
  Phase Shift charges, stored teleports and Extra Life lives already granted;
  only the level reverts. Assert for `extra_life` (lives count unchanged after
  the window closes), `phase_shift` (charges unchanged, recharge pool intact)
  and `teleport` (stored uses unchanged). Also assert the consumables
  themselves never carry a timer (no expiry after a long tick).
- **Choice and HUD semantics unchanged (AC5).** The hold-full choice still
  prices the permanent level only (no temporary inflation, no `★ New`
  regression for a permanently-owned item). HUD rows: effective level in the
  label, a live countdown while a window is open for the newly-windowed kinds
  (`bomb`, `smart_bomb`, `strike`, and the UFO/charge kinds where a row is
  visible), and `∞` afterwards. A field-only pickup of a one-shot kind still
  leaves no HUD row (existing rule).
- **Slot accounting follows expiry (AC6).** A temporary stack's six-slot
  occupancy is released when its window expires for **every** kind, including
  the seven instant kinds: `getTempPowerUpIds()` no longer lists the kind and
  the derived slot count drops by one. A permanently-owned kind keeps its slot.

Only make production changes where a test exposes a real gap — the expected
outcome is that AC4/AC6 fall out of the store/registry behaviour once AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ lands,
and AC5 needs at most a row-visibility tweak.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Consumables persist.** Extra Life lives, Phase Shift charges and
  Teleport uses already granted by a temporary pickup survive the level revert
  (only the level reverts), and the consumables themselves never expire.
  Tests assert both the revert and the retained counts, and that a long tick
  does not consume them.
- AC2 — **Choice and HUD semantics unchanged.** The hold-full choice still
  offers and permanent-prices the permanent level only (no temporary
  inflation, no `★ New` regression) before and after a temporary window on the
  same kind.
- AC3 — HUD tests assert, for the newly windowed kinds that show a row: a live
  countdown while the window is open, `∞` after expiry, and no new row for a
  field-only one-shot pickup.
- AC4 — **Slot accounting follows expiry.** A temporary stack releases its
  six-slot occupancy when its window expires for every kind, including the
  seven instant kinds (plus a timed control kind), while a permanently-owned
  kind keeps its slot.
- AC5 — Any production change is minimal and justified by a failing test
  recorded in the work-item comments (expected: none for the consumable and
  slot assertions).

## Constraints

- Do not add a "consumed consumables" rollback path; consumables are never
  clawed back.
- Do not change `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` or the available-when-full exemption rules.
- Reuse the derived snapshots (`getTempPowerUpIds`, `getLevels`) rather than
  introducing new occupancy counters.

## Key Files

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts` — consumable persistence on
  `clearTemporary`.
- `src/powerups/choice.test.ts` — permanent-only pricing unchanged.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — countdown/`∞`/row-visibility assertions.
- `src/powerups/slots.test.ts` — occupancy released on expiry per kind.
- `src/powerups/slots.parity.test.ts` — parity of derived occupancy.
- `src/powerups/__tests__/temporaryRevert.test.ts` — AH-0MVUGI3BF00423OO table extensions.

## Related work

- Parent: AH-0MVSTKGC3003OMAC (AC4, AC5, AC6, Resolved decision 2).
- Depends on: AH-0MVUGI448000GNMJ (windows exist for the instant kinds) and AH-0MVUGI4IC006PUS5 (no stranded
  stacks).

## Problem

Candidate D's *States* section (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § Candidate D → States) defines a ring win as **all six hexes held and the AI's massed counter-attack on the hangar repelled**, and a campaign loss as **the hangar falls** (the last hex taken and the hangar's own defence failing). The MVP build (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE) deliberately ships the narrower rule, decided by the producer on 2026-10-30 (intake question Q2 = a):

- **Ring secured = every hex of the current ring held.** The next ring then opens.
- **No massed hangar assault** is resolved or played.
- **No hangar-falls lose state**: the hangar itself can never be lost in the MVP, so a player cannot lose the campaign.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the ring to end with a real fight for the hangar — a massed AI counter-attack I have to repel, and a defeat condition that means the hangar can actually fall — so that holding the whole ring feels like a victory rather than the start of the next checklist.

## Desired change

- When the last hex of a ring is captured, **resolve an algorithmic hangar assault** from stored numbers (defender ratings of the held ring vs. the AI's massed force scaled by frontier aggression) — no live simulated battle, matching Candidate D's algorithmic-resolution rule.
- A repelled assault = the ring win state (existing) **plus** a legible report of the numbers.
- A failed assault = **the hangar falls**: define the consequence (restart the current ring with the hangar's unlocks kept, or a documented alternative) and make the reset legible in the defence report.
- Record the chosen win/lose semantics in GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`.
- Pure resolver logic, exercised in the existing `GymHexWar` gym; gym↔game parity per AGENTS.md; attract mode must not stall (no live battle).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Capturing the ring's final hex triggers an algorithmic hangar-assault resolution from stored numbers, with a report showing the numbers that produced the result.
2. A repelled assault marks the ring won; a failed assault applies the documented hangar-falls consequence.
3. The resolver is a pure module exercised in the gym, with unit tests for repel, fall and boundary cases, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` updated if the gym surface changes.
4. The attract bot traverses or skips the assault report without stalling.
5. GDD §8 and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` record the win/lose semantics; build and full suite green; all related documentation updated.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Context

Deferred by producer decision during intake of AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE (2026-10-30, question Q2 = a). Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (States, Minimal first slice) and GDD §8.

# Goal

As a player, I want a hangar screen where I can see what I own, buy the next
useful unlock and choose the hull and loadout I deploy with, so that "what I own"
and "what I hold" sit one click apart instead of becoming admin.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase A.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § UI / scene
  surface — "the hangar screen (Candidate B's unlock tree) … a deployment /
  hull-and-loadout selector on the way into a hex"; and § Attract mode — "in the
  hangar it auto-buys the cheapest useful unlock (seeded)".
- Style and navigation precedents: `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/LeaderboardScene.ts`, `src/utils/focusManager.ts` (Tab/arrow focus,
  Enter/Space activation), GDD §7.1 neon palette; `GymHangar` (A1) is the
  scenario harness.
- Risk to mitigate: "two progressions, twice the bookkeeping" — this screen is
  the mitigation, so it must be legible at a glance.

## Scope

- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`: unlock tree (cost, owned, gated), salvage balance,
  hull selection and loadout selection, keyboard + pointer navigation through the
  shared `FocusManager`.
- All state goes through the hangar-war store and the pure economy module — no
  purchase logic in the scene.
- `GymHangar` renders the same screen code path against an injected payload, and
  the attract bot decision for this screen (auto-buy cheapest useful unlock,
  accept the loadout) lands here.

## Tests first

Scene tests for rendering from an injected payload, purchase-through-store,
keyboard focus/activation and the bot's auto-buy before the visual polish.

## Key Files

- new: `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` (+ test)
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts`, `src/utils/focusManager.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on A4 (economy) and A1 (GymHangar harness).
- Prerequisite for the map screen (B4) and the defence report (B6), which link
  back to the hangar.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hangar screen renders the unlock tree and a deployment/loadout selector
  (hull, starting weapons, modifiers) in the shipped neon palette, with keyboard
  focus navigation and pointer support.
- The screen reads and writes only through the hangar-war store and the pure
  economy module — no duplicated purchase logic in scene code (the equivalence
  guard does not flag a copied helper body).
- `GymHangar` exercises the same screen code path with an injected payload, and
  the attract bot can auto-buy the cheapest useful unlock and pick a deployment
  loadout without stalling.
- Unaffordable and already-owned entries are visibly disabled and cannot be
  activated by keyboard or pointer; tests cover both.

# Goal

As the producer, I want proof that the hangar slice stands alone as a complete
outer loop before any ring work starts, so that if the ring disappoints in play
Candidate B still ships and no work is wasted.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase A gate.
This is the verification item that closes phase A end to end.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` *Minimal first slice* — "If
  'take a hex, leave a bot, buy a hull, retake what the AI stole' already feels
  like a war worth fighting, more rings can follow; if it does not, B alone
  stands (the slice is a strict superset of B's, so nothing is wasted)"; and
  *Recommendation* — "Ship it in B's shape first."
- Prior children: A1 harness, A2 store, A3 salvage banking, A4 economy, A5 hangar
  scene, A6 menu entry + deployment.

## Scope

- An end-to-end test that walks the whole hangar slice with an injected
  `localStorage`: deploy → reach a checkpoint (bank) → die (only unbanked
  salvage lost) → buy an unlock → deploy again with the new hull/loadout.
- A regression assertion that the shipped game is untouched: classic campaign
  start, checkpoint/Continue semantics, leaderboard, settings, six shared
  loadout slots, Extra Life and Mystery UFO.
- A short written record (work-item comment) of what the slice proves and any gap
  deferred to phase B.
- **Phase A documentation** (so the phase is a vertical slice, not a horizontal
  layer): GDD §8 gains the hangar-slice specification (entry surface and mode
  separation, hangar economy and unlock tree, salvage banking at checkpoint
  moments, the `ai_hell_hangar_war` key and migration note) and `README.md`
  mentions the Hangar War mode. The ring specification is added later by B8.
- If an end-to-end gap is found that blocks the slice, file it as a child of this
  item rather than widening it.

## Tests first

The end-to-end and regression tests are written against the shipped slice
behaviour and must fail before any gap they expose is fixed.

## Key Files

- new: `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarSlice.integration.test.ts`
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/`

## Dependencies

- Depends on A3, A4, A5 and A6 (all of phase A).
- Gates phase B: B1 (ring harness) must not start until this passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Hangar slice first (Candidate B's MVP).** Banked salvage (minerals +
  mini-boss cores at the existing checkpoint moments), a persistent hangar with
  one extra hull, three unlockable starting weapons, one permanent modifier, and
  a deployment/loadout selector; losing a run forfeits only that run's unbanked
  salvage.
- An end-to-end integration test proves the full slice cycle (deploy → bank →
  lose → buy → redeploy) against an injected storage, with only unbanked salvage
  lost on death.
- The shipped game is unchanged: classic campaign start, checkpoint/Continue,
  leaderboard, settings, six loadout slots, Extra Life and Mystery UFO all pass
  their existing suites unmodified.
- GDD §8 and `README.md` document the shipped hangar slice (entry surface, hangar
  economy, salvage banking, persistence key and migration note), so phase A is a
  vertical slice through code, tests and docs rather than a horizontal layer.
- `npm run build` and the changed-scope gate pass, and the slice's remaining gaps
  (if any) are recorded on the work item.

# Goal

As a player, I want a between-sortie defence report that tells me which of my
hexes were attacked, which held and which fell, and the exact numbers behind each
result — and as a demo watcher I never want attract mode to stall on a defence or
on a new screen.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § UI / scene
  surface (the between-sortie defence report) and § Attract mode ("the bot
  traverses or skips every new screen — on the map it auto-picks the **weakest**
  adjacent hex, in the hangar it auto-buys the cheapest useful unlock, and it
  auto-advances the defence report. Because defence is resolved algorithmically,
  there is no live defence battle for the demo to stall in").
- Failure modes to mitigate: *opaque defence* ("a hex falls and the player cannot
  see why … show the numbers (defender rating vs. attacking force)") and *the
  frontier treadmill* (an answerable tick, shown).
- Today there is no scene-to-scene menu traversal in demo mode — the demo boots
  straight into `PlayScene` — so the traversal here is new behaviour
  (`src/ai/`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`).

## Scope

- `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts`: per-hex rows from the resolver's per-tick
  record — attacking force, aggression, defender rating, outcome, margin, and
  what it would take to retake the hex — plus a continue action back to the map.
- Frontier tick integration: the tick runs between runs (on returning from a
  deployment) and its record feeds this screen.
- Attract-mode traversal for the whole new surface: menu → map → (weakest hex)
  deployment → defence report → map → hangar (cheapest useful unlock), driven by
  pure, tested bot decisions with seeded choices; no live defence battle exists to
  stall in.

## Tests first

Report-rendering tests from a synthetic tick record and a full traversal
integration test (bot drives every new screen without stalling) before the scene
and bot wiring.

## Key Files

- new: `src/scenes/DefenceReportScene.ts` (+ test), traversal decisions in
  `src/ai/` (+ tests)
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
  `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B3 (tick record), B5 (between-run wiring) and A5 (hangar).
- Prerequisite for timing validation (B7).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The defence report shows the numbers that produced every result: per hex the
  attacking force, aggression, defender rating, hold/fall outcome, margin and what
  it would take to retake it, generated from the resolver's per-tick record.
- **Attract mode never stalls.** The demo bot traverses or skips the map, hangar
  and defence report (auto-pick weakest hex, auto-buy cheapest useful unlock) and
  there is no live defence battle to stall in.
- An integration test drives menu → map → deployment → defence report → map →
  hangar with the bot and asserts every screen advances within a bounded time and
  no defence battle is ever simulated.
- The report is a pure view over the tick record and the stored payload — the same
  code path runs in `GymHexWar`, with no gameplay rule in the scene.
data.title: Between-sortie defence report and attract-mode traversal

# Goal

As the producer, I want the ring's play time and playstyle trade-off measured
rather than guessed — ring 1 at 40–60 minutes and ring 2 at ≈70–100 minutes for a
semi-skilled player, with the rush line faster-but-riskier and the grind line
safer-but-slower — so the ring lands as an evening's play and neither strategy is
strictly dominant.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B.

## Context

- Design of record: `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Session shape
  ("the **one-ring MVP targets 40–60 minutes** … **Ring 2 is larger — 12 hexes** —
  so it lands at … **≈70–100 minutes**") and § Playstyles supported ("No style is
  strictly dominant — the aggressive line is **faster but riskier** and slow
  grinding is **safer but slower**, which is the intended trade").
- Intake assumption A1: timing is measured with the existing headless eval arena —
  `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` reports per-run `durationSeconds` / `ticksSimulated`, so
  a ring's play time is summed from simulated deployments rather than guessed. No
  new instrumentation is required.
- Intake assumption Q4: the headless arena is sufficient evidence for the
  recorded target; a human playtest is desirable but not a gate.

## Scope

- A headless ring-timing harness (a thin driver over `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) that
  simulates a ring's deployments at their resolved aggression and sums
  `durationSeconds`, plus a modelled build/retry allowance so the budget covers
  the whole ring rather than deployments alone.
- Two strategy simulations: **rush** (weapon hex first, then push into the next
  ring) and **grind** (secure the ring before pushing); record deployments,
  losses, salvage and wall-clock minutes for each.
- Tuning of aggression growth, defender ratings and grant strengths so both
  budgets and both strategies land in range; record the measured numbers,
  method and confidence in the GDD §8 timings section (B8 writes the prose; this
  item supplies the numbers) and on the work item.
- Any budget miss beyond tolerance raises a child item rather than silently
  widening the target.

## Tests first

A deterministic timing-harness test (same seed → same summed duration) and a
budget-assertion test with an explicit tolerance before tuning.

## Key Files

- new: `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` (+ test / CLI entry), ring timing fixtures
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/data/hex-ring-1.csv`, `src/data/hex-ring-2.csv`,
  `src/data/frontier-tuning.json`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B6 (the whole ring loop, including the between-run tick).
- Prerequisite for the docs item (B8).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Timing targets.** One-ring MVP is completable in 40–60 minutes by a
  semi-skilled player; ring 2 (12 hexes) lands at ≈70–100 minutes; the timing is
  recorded in the GDD and measured with the headless eval arena
  (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts` per-run durations, summed per ring).
- **Playstyles supported.** A rush through the weapon hex into the next ring, and
  a full grind of the ring before pushing, are both viable and neither is strictly
  dominant; the difficulty curve makes the aggressive line riskier but faster.
- The timing harness is deterministic (same seed and payload → same summed
  duration, asserted by a test) and a budget test asserts both ring windows with a
  stated tolerance.
- The measured numbers, strategy comparison and method are recorded on the work
  item for the docs item to publish.
data.title: Ring timing validation and playstyle balance

# Goal

As a player and maintainer, I want the Hangar War documented as a playable
specification and its build status recorded, so the docs of record (GDD §8,
`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md`) describe what
now ships rather than what was proposed.

Part of **Build Candidate D — Hangar War (AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE)**, phase B, and the
build's final gate.

## Context

- GDD §8 currently records "the **decision and the design intent only**: it is not
  a playable specification, and no candidate's gameplay, persistence-schema or
  scene implementation is specified here. The specification and implementation
  land through AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE."
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D says "**Design only, not
  scheduled.**" and needs a build-status update.
- Guarded docs: `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` (gym rows),
  `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts` (candidates document assertions),
  `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts` / `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` (new
  watchable gym scenes).
- **`CHANGELOG.md` is owned by the ship skill — do not edit it.**

## Scope

- GDD §8: replace the design-intent note with a **playable Hangar War
  specification** — entry surface and mode separation, the hangar and its
  economy, the hex ring and ring growth, the capture cycle, the defence resolver
  and frontier tick (with the actual numbers), the defence report, the measured
  ring timings and the supported playstyles — while keeping the decision record.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`: Candidate D build status (implemented /
  shipped), deferred post-MVP items and their work items.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`: refresh `GymHangar` and `GymHexWar` rows (enabled objects,
  spawn seam, inherited loop, divergences).
- `README.md`: player-facing description of the Hangar War mode and its
  persistence key.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`: the two new watchable gym scenes.
- Code comments where behaviour is non-obvious (resolver maths, ring generator,
  mode isolation).

## Tests first

Docs assertions are already test-guarded; extend the existing docs tests
(`outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts`,
`multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts`) to pin the new specification sections before
writing the prose.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §8, `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md`,
  `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `README.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`
- docs tests: `src/outerLoopCandidatesDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`, `src/multiSceneCaptureDocs.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Depends on B7 (measured timing numbers) and therefore on the whole ring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Build and full suite green**, and the docs/code comments updated.
- GDD §8 records the playable Hangar War specification (entry surface, hangar
  economy, ring model and growth, capture cycle, resolver and frontier tick with
  the real numbers, defence report, measured ring timings, supported playstyles)
  and keeps the producer decision record.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` records Candidate D's build status and the
  deferred post-MVP items with their work-item ids; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` carries
  current `GymHangar`/`GymHexWar` rows; `README.md` and
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` describe the new mode and scenes.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched (owned by the ship skill), and the docs tests
  (`outerLoopCandidatesDocs`, `gymParityDocs`, `multiSceneCaptureDocs`) pin the new
  specification.
